solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Guy on rounds called about collecting uniforms

indicators.note: collecting means the turned word gathers the uniforms inside itself
about means the word for called is turned round to face the other way

parts.note: to be called something is to be named
livery is the uniform worn by servants or company staff

explanation.surface: A man doing his rounds was called up over some uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a name or a verb; it is just a man. 'about' turns the word for called round, and 'collecting' puts the uniforms inside it, giving DEMAN around the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery man is a fellow whose job takes him on a regular round dropping off goods.

clue.text: Reverse order to sanction modern reading material

indicators.note: Reverse tells the solver to read the letters of the order backwards

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour
to sanction something is to OK it, give it approval

explanation.surface: An instruction to cancel an order so as to approve some new reading matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' turns OBE (an honour, Order of the British Empire) into EBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital book read on a screen is today's form of the printed volume.

clue.text: I didn't know that: (i) the outfit I just bought was second-hand; …

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise at hearing something unfamiliar

definitions.text: the outfit I just bought was second-hand
definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase says this item of clothing is new to me and is being worn by me, though not new

explanation.surface: Someone surprised to learn that their newly bought outfit was used.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses chain this clue to the next two: all three answers are phrases meaning 'I didn't know that', and each has its own wordplay after its numbered part.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for meeting something unknown before; worn literally, a used garment is still fresh to its wearer.

clue.text: … (ii) original Yale discovery had soya in the mix; …

indicators.note: original here means made into something fresh, so the letters are reworked
in the mix says these letters are stirred together with the others

explanation.surface: A researcher at Yale finds soya was part of a blend.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the shared 'I didn't know that' at the start of the 3 down clue. 'original' and 'in the mix' together signal rearranging all the letters of YALE DISCOVERY and HAD SOYA.
explanation.definitionFit: The ellipsis carries over the shared stem of 3 down, 'I didn't know that', and this saying admits learning something fresh.

clue.text: … (iii) story will captivate naked souls, given candles

indicators.note: will captivate says the story will hold the other letters inside it

parts.note: a yarn is a tale or story

indicators.note: naked means each of the three words is stripped of its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A tale holds stripped souls in thrall, given candlelight.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the definition from the start of 3 down. 'naked' strips SOULS, GIVEN and CANDLES to their middles, which 'will captivate' puts inside the story.
explanation.definitionFit: The ellipsis carries over the shared stem of 3 down, 'I didn't know that', and this saying shrugs off a fresh lesson.

clue.text: Like naysayers, only some meant it

indicators.note: only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only a few of those who said no truly meant it.
explanation.definitionFit: People who keep saying no are opposed to things, which is what the prefix-word means.

clue.text: Challenge up-and-coming swinging bar can do

indicators.note: swinging suggests movement, so the letters are thrown around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, its letters are the pool
these are the letters to be removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A promising new bar with swinging music proves it can do the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' means except: take the letters of CAN DO (AND and CO) out of UP-AND-COMING, leaving UPMING, which 'swinging' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To challenge a claim is to call it into question or dispute it.

clue.text: So many contenders to sort out, follows the form

indicators.note: to sort out a jumble means putting its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A selector faces a crowd of contenders, guided by form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' in the surface suggests racing form or past performance; here it means etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists on formality and correct etiquette sticks to the proper conventions.

clue.text: Mickey maybe wants a second taste of summer pudding

indicators.note: wants a second says the word already has one S and needs another put into it

parts.note: Mickey is the famous Disney cartoon mouse

indicators.note: a taste of something is just a little of it, here its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone asking for another helping of summer pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Summer pudding is a British dessert of bread and soft fruit, a red herring here.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped dessert is a type of sweet course, often called afters in Britain.

clue.text: Poles struck in last minute, enlivening final

indicators.note: enlivening stirs these letters up into a livelier arrangement
struck means crossed off, so these letters are deleted

parts.note: the North and South poles are N and S

explanation.surface: A last-minute strike by Polish players livens up a final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struck' removes S and N from LAST MINUTE, leaving LATMIUTE, which 'enlivening' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is last in a series is the end point, the very last.

clue.text: Heading for sea, go off bar clothes for year-round bathing

definitions.text: Heading for sea, go off bar clothes for year-round bathing

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the next word
bathing here means sitting immersed in, so these letters go inside the sleep word

parts.note: to go off is to fall asleep, to kip
an inn is a pub, somewhere with a bar

indicators.note: clothes for means the outside letters dress the word, so take its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone heading off to the sea to swim naked all year round.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer. 'clothes for' gives the first and last letters of YEAR-ROUND; 'bathing' puts those, after the bar, inside the sleep word, all after the sea's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimming naked means bathing without any clothes on, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Pigment line dropped by fashion house acquiring northern corporation

indicators.note: acquiring means the shortened brand takes the other letters into itself
dropped by says the line is lost from the fashion house's name

parts.note: Burberry is a British fashion house
RY, short for railway, is a line
corporation is an old jokey word for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A fashion house loses a product line after buying a northern company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped by' takes the railway line out of the brand, leaving BURBER; 'acquiring' puts the other letters inside. Corporation for a pot belly is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark brown earth colour used by painters, made by roasting a natural clay.

clue.text: See 4
Boat business in the Falmouth area?

indicators.note: in places the business abbreviation inside the area letters

parts.note: Falmouth is a port in Cornwall, in the South West (SW) of England
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A question about boats used for trade around a Cornish port.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed barge used for carrying cargo is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: See 8
To move third base closer to second, state understands reluctance

indicators.text: To move third base closer to second
indicators.note: base is E, the base of natural logarithms; the third E in the letters steps one place towards the second E

parts.note: to state is to aver, assert
to understand is to sense

explanation.surface: Baseball talk: shifting third base nearer second, a state reveals its reluctance.
explanation.walkthrough: AVER plus SENSES gives AVERSENSES with E's at the third, sixth and ninth places; moving the last one up a place gives the answer. 'base' looks like baseball but is the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwillingness or disinclination, being averse to something.

clue.text: After many others sound tremulous, sharing a cell with Athlan and Thimba?

parts.note: to trill is to make a quavering, tremulous sound

indicators.note: sharing a cell with means the two words share one letter where they meet, so one L is dropped

parts.note: Aslan and Simba, two famous fictional lions, said with a lisp, give lions spoken lisping

explanation.surface: A prisoner trembles, sharing a cell with two oddly named inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: TRILL and LIONTH overlap on one L. Aslan (Narnia) and Simba (The Lion King) are lions; Athlan and Thimba are their names lisped.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal of a million million comes after an enormous number of predecessors.

clue.text: Compilers bet that Spooner's given wiggle room

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: the setters writing as a group would call themselves we
to lay a bet is to wager

explanation.surface: Puzzle setters wager that Spooner was allowed some slack.
explanation.walkthrough: WE LAY with the opening sounds swapped becomes LEE WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom to act or margin for error, originally drift of a ship downwind.

clue.text: Orwell's excuse for not writing part of the dialogue in Animal Farm?

definitions.text: Orwell's excuse for not writing part of the dialogue in Animal Farm?

parts.words: Orwell's excuse for not writing part of the dialogue in Animal Farm?
parts.note: a pig's grunt in the fable, jokily split as the zero-letter plus the pen's fluid: with nothing to write with, the author has his excuse

explanation.surface: Why George Orwell never finished some of the talk in his farmyard fable.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as O (nothing) plus INK: having no ink is an excuse for not writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise a pig makes, and pigs do much of the talking in Orwell's fable.

clue.text: See 3
See 12
Catching on, clues of Flimsy are glowing

indicators.note: catching means the jumbled letters hold another word inside them
flimsy suggests something loosely made, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: RE is Latin for about, on the subject of

explanation.surface: Clues written by someone called Flimsy are catching on and shining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flimsy' rearranges CLUES OF into FLUOSCE, and 'Catching' places RE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To give off light when exposed to radiation is to shine with a cold light, as the plural verb needs.

clue.text: In May, taxmen stone heap

indicators.note: In places the taxmen inside the word for May

parts.note: may and can both mean being allowed to
IR is the old Inland Revenue, the British tax authority

explanation.surface: In May, tax inspectors arrive at a pile of stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound of stones built as a landmark or memorial on a hill.

clue.text: Indian city hotel is wanting specialist food outlet

indicators.note: is wanting means the city name is lacking a letter

parts.note: Delhi is the city in northern India
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Indian city hotel lacks a specialist food shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared and imported fine foods.

clue.text: Secret door to Burlington House opened, and?

parts.note: when a door is opened, what happens next: someone in came
Burlington House in London is home of the Royal Academy, RA, which also stands for a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A hidden door into the Royal Academy's building swings open, and then?
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House is the London home of the Royal Academy of Arts; when its door opened, in came an RA (Royal Academician).
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'in a chamber', used of court hearings held in private.

clue.text: Exhausted Merz's refusal to attend function

indicators.note: to attend means to follow or wait upon, so this word comes after

parts.note: a do is a party or function
Friedrich Merz is German chancellor, and nein is German for no

explanation.surface: The German chancellor declines an invitation to a function, tired out.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out, completely tired, as an idiom.

clue.text: Lectin carriers damaged skin, probed by western A&E prior to demise

indicators.note: probed by means the jumbled skin letters have the next group pushed into them
damaged means the letters are knocked into a new arrangement
western, in an across clue, means read from right to left

parts.note: A and E taken as letters
by can mean before, as in by tomorrow
demise is the end

explanation.surface: A patient with damaged skin is examined in casualty before dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' makes KINS; 'western' turns the reversed run into DNEYBEA, which 'probed by' pushes inside. A&E (accident and emergency) is the British hospital casualty department.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw red beans contain a toxic lectin, so these pulses carry it.
